candidates.title: JEP 545 Moves ZGC Memory Preparation off the Startup Path in JDK 28
candidates.excerpt: JEP 545, Faster Startup and Warmup with ZGC, has been integrated into JDK 28, moving heap memory preparation onto concurrent worker threads. ZGC now pre-touches memory as it expands and upgrades small pages to large ones on Linux 6.1 and later, but the 2 MB initial heap behind the JEP's 38% startup and 90% warmup gains requires the adaptive heap sizing flag from JEP 546, which is off by default. By A N M Bazlur Rahman

The team wrote 45 architecture decision records for people and agents, added a review agent that posts only verified blockers, and serves per-domain GraphRAG context through a single MCP tool. By Andrew Hoblitzell

candidates.title: Agoda Reduces API Code Review Time by 64% with Modular Architecture

Framework-backed changes showed 64% shorter median code reviews and 34% faster initial feedback than legacy changes. By Leela Kumili

candidates.title: Podcast: Simulation Can Tell You What Your Agents are Actually Doing: A Conversation with Zhou Yu
candidates.excerpt: Michael Stiefel spoke to Zhou Yu about using dynamic simulations to evaluate AI agents. One particular focus was conversational agents where actions depend on prior responses, and the non-deterministic nation of LLMs means you cannot rely on static, reference-based benchmarks. You need to test them using dynamic simulations that incorporate different personas, goals, and corner cases. By Zhou Yu

candidates.title: QCon San Francisco 2026: The Harness Is the New Operating System

The keynote mapped the parts of a harness, including context, tools, state, permissions and feedback loops, onto jobs that operating systems already perform. By Andrew Hoblitzell
